records.headline: FAA AD 2025-25-12 mandates A350 flight-control software update (FCRM hydraulic-fluid contamination)
records.summary: FAA AD 2025-25-12, effective 13 January 2026, requires all A350-900/-1000 operators to install updated Flight Control and Guidance System software (PRIM P14.1.3 / SEC S14.1.2) to permanently close out a risk of uncommanded control-surface movement caused by hydraulic-fluid contamination of Flight Control Remote Module (FCRM) electronic cards. It supersedes the interim AD 2025-13-12 (July 2025) and incorporates EASA AD 2025-0197R1.

references.ref_number: FAA AD 2025-25-12 (supersedes AD 2025-13-12); incorporates EASA AD 2025-0197R1
references.effectivity: All Airbus A350-900 and A350-1000 series airplanes

records.oem_regulator_position: Reported: software fix is positioned by Airbus/FAA as the permanent mitigation, replacing interim hardware-replacement program.
records.root_cause: Reported: hydraulic fluid contaminated an FCRM electronic card, which could cause uncommanded movement of an outboard aileron (and by shared design, elevator/rudder) surface.
records.verifier_notes: Effective date (2026-01-13) and Federal Register publication (2025-12-29) are both outside the 30-day lookback window. Flagged as developing/standing carryover only because it is a fleet type and a major compliance item; verifier should confirm whether it is still 'new' to this digest run or already reported in a prior week.

records.headline: FAA AD requires replacement of GE90 HPT stage 1/2 disks for iron-inclusion powder-metal defect
records.summary: FAA adopted a new AD (Federal Register doc 2025-24173, docket FAA-2025-1364), published 2 January 2026 and effective 6 February 2026, requiring replacement of GE90-90B/-94B/-110B1/-115B HPT stage 1 and stage 2 disks suspected of iron-inclusion contamination in the powder-metal manufacturing process, which can cause reduced fatigue life and premature/uncontained disk fracture. GE90-115B powers the CX 777-300ER fleet.

records.root_cause: Reported: HPT stage 1/2 disks manufactured from powder metal material suspected to contain iron inclusion, attributed to a manufacturing process deficiency, reducing fatigue life and raising risk of premature fracture / uncontained failure.

records.headline: FAA AD (effective June 8, 2026) on A330 standby fuel pump dormant failure / trapped fuel
records.summary: FAA adopted a new AD (Federal Register doc 2026-10272, docket FAA-2026-4641), effective 8 June 2026, for all Airbus A330-200/-200F/-300/-841/-941 series airplanes after an in-service event found that a dormant standby fuel pump failure could trap an unusable quantity of fuel in the aft section of the inner tank. The AD requires repetitive operational checks of standby fuel pumps and corrective action, and limits installation of affected parts.

records.headline: A320-family ELAC software AD (solar-radiation pitch event) — FAA final rule effective Jan 2026, ongoing fleet remediation
records.summary: Following a JetBlue A320 uncommanded pitch-down event on 30 October 2025 attributed to intense solar radiation (coronal mass ejection) corrupting an Elevator Aileron Computer (ELAC B, L104 software standard), EASA issued emergency AD 2025-0268-E (effective 29 Nov 2025) and the FAA issued a mirroring emergency AD effective 6 January 2026, both requiring reversion to ELAC B L103+ or replacement, affecting up to ~6,000 A320/A320neo-family aircraft worldwide. Long-term, Airbus has stated radiation-hardened ELAC upgrades are planned for 2026 production.

references.ref_number: EASA AD 2025-0268-E; FAA AD (FR doc 2025-24242, published 2026-01-05)
references.effectivity: Airbus A319/A320/A321 series including A321neo (-251NX, -252NX, -253NX, -271NX, -272NX etc.)

records.root_cause: Reported: extreme solar radiation from a coronal mass ejection interfered with ELAC processing, causing an uncommanded, limited pitch-down event.
records.read_across: Directly involves the A321neo's flight-control computer family (ELAC), shared across the wider A320/A321neo line CX operates; software standard/hardware revision status of CX's own A321neo fleet should be checked.
records.verifier_notes: Effective dates fall outside the 30-day window but this is a major, still-resolving fleet-wide A320/A321 family issue with direct relevance to the A321neo; flagged developing_carryover. records.headline: NTSB UPS MD-11 (Flight 2976) crash investigation — May 2026 hearings detail aft-pylon bearing fatigue cracking
records.summary: NTSB held investigative hearings (19-21 May 2026, docket DCA26MA024) into the 4 November 2025 crash of UPS Flight 2976, an MD-11F that lost its No.1 engine/pylon on takeoff from Louisville, killing 15. Hearings revealed fatigue cracking in an aft pylon spherical bearing (P/N S00399-1), at least 10 prior in-service bearing-failure incidents (only 4 formally reported to FAA), and a 2011 Boeing service letter (MD-11-SL-54-104-A) that recommended but did not mandate replacement. The FAA's emergency AD 2025-23-53 grounded MD-11/DC-10/MD-10 variants; FAA approved a Boeing inspection/maintenance protocol ending the grounding on 11 May 2026.

references.ref_number: NTSB docket DCA26MA024 — Aircraft Accident Investigative Update

records.oem_regulator_position: Reported: Boeing staff acknowledged at the hearing that the failed aft pylon spherical bearing should have been classified as a Principal Structural Element during original MD-11 certification.
records.root_cause: Reported (NTSB investigative update): fatigue cracking originating in a lubrication channel / design recess groove inside the bearing race, propagating around the circumference until overstress fracture of both lugs.
records.read_across: Classic 'UPS MD-11 class' major industry event — pylon/engine-mount structural integrity and OEM service-letter-vs-mandatory-AD gap is a generic read-across theme for all CX fleet types' continuing operational safety / aging-component monitoring programs, even though CX operates no MD-11/DC-10.
records.verifier_notes: Hearing dates (May 19-21, 2026) are just outside the 30-day window (window starts 2026-05-28) but this is the canonical 'major industry event of broad significance' the project charter calls out by name; carry over as developing. Verifier should check for any NTSB update published since 2026-05-28.
